steps.name: Club Owner
steps.text: Experimental rock, one vote... acid jazz, one vote...

steps.name: Club Owner
steps.text: ...Death metal, one vote.

steps.name: Club Owner
steps.text: Same thing as yesterday, folks. We still don't have a genre set for this week's theme.

steps.name: Club Owner
steps.text: Debate time starts... now.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Sullivan! You promised me you would vote for death metal after watching that black box performance!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: But the freedom of electronic music is the sound of the future!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: I'll pay you back for your ticket—

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Once I've sold my new work.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: You really think the price of two measly tickets can match the everlasting impression that incredible concert left on your soul?

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Change your vote.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Street Sculptor
steps.text: I'm afraid that's not possible.

steps.name: Street Sculptor
steps.text: To stop people from adding votes on their own, the boss told me to make the scoreboard from metal this time.

steps.name: Street Sculptor
steps.text: The boss gave me a budget, so I had to make do with the harder, cheaper kind. Only problem is, I need to use an electric drill to write the scores.
*sound of drilling*

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Seriously though, shouldn't we just stop with the voting at this point?

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Rigged voting boxes, voice-controlled score panels, even attempted mass hypnosis... the cheating methods get more outlandish and scarier each time.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Last time, 'Maestro' juggled ten pieces of Originite Prime in one hand to draw our attention while changing the score with the other hand, just so Leithanian folk music would win.

steps.name: Club Owner
steps.text: The scariest part is that it worked.

steps.name: Street Sculptor
steps.text: Which is why 'Maestro' doesn't get to nominate anymore.
*sound of drilling*

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Huh? What did you say?

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: One vote... Just one vote, again...

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: It's just like it was back underground.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: No one understands my taste in art! I can't take it anymore!

steps.name: Club Owner
steps.text: Come on, Tecno, don't be angry, you're my favorite customer.

steps.name: Club Owner
steps.text: But a community has to have rules. You know how hard it is to get these avant-garde artists to play nice with each other.

steps.name: Club Owner
steps.text: Even if your choice of music doesn't win, everybody's artwork gets to be displayed in the club for free, including your little puppet.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: I know...

steps.name: Club Owner
steps.text: Besides, well, death metal is a little—

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: A little what?!
*sound of drilling*

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Knock it off, Sculptor! You can tally later!
*sound of drilling*... ecno... Tecno... wake up...

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Who is it this time? You'll do anything to keep me from winning, huh?
...most of the fire has been extinguished... removing beams... passed out from smoke inhalation...

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Hey, do you smell that?

steps.name: Firefighter
steps.text: ...Tecno! Can you hear me, Tecno?!

steps.name: Firefighter
steps.text: I warned you kids to keep flammables away from the wires. The wiring in the club is a mess!

steps.name: Firefighter
steps.text: What am I saying... it's my fault. I should've known you wouldn't throw away your artwork.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: ...Diaz...? Papá?

steps.name: Diaz
steps.text: Bueno, you're awake! Paramedics will be here soon. I'm so glad you weren't badly hurt.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Death metal... theme day...

steps.name: Diaz
steps.text: Don't speak. You need rest.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Sullivan... Jefe... The others...

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: We're here at the scene of the fire.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Firefighters are on site, but rescue efforts are taking longer than expected due to the remote location.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: As the fire spreads, residents in the local community are trying to fight it on their own. Let's interview some of the people affected.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Hello. Condolences on your loss. Do you know how the fire started?

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Save the condolences. Shut your mouth and do something useful!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Nobody ever cared about fires in this community. We've never had reporters like you in here before.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: It seems this community has been a fire risk for many years. Frequent fires, abandoned scrap... all have a significant impact on the surrounding areas.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: What are you getting at?

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: The fire has nothing to do with our art!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: It's true that we have to resort to scavenging scrap for our artwork because we don't have the money, but that doesn't mean we put any less artistic expression into it.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: These street artists have no care or concern for the public. Despite knowing full well that their work is completely worthless, they continue to act with the extreme selfishness that has led to this tragedy—

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: I'll teach you to talk like that!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Uh... Despite their failure as artists, it seems their true talent lies in violence. It's hard to fathom how this group of unkempt vagrants claims to be artists.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Sullivan! Stop! He's trying to provoke you. This is live TV.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Did you forget how media spin lost us our only sponsor?

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: I know! But I just can't stand these people coming to jeer at us at a time like this!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: The club just got renovated. We painted the wall brush by brush.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: That Originium kinetic device next to the bar cost Sculptor two years of savings. It was going to an exhibition next month, might even get its own column in Art Review... but now?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Ahem... these hoodlums have intentionally placed flammable items such as paper, wood, and Originium products beneath aging circuitry, perhaps as some kind of perverted 'artistic expression'.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Without proper oversight, however, such disasters will only continue to repeat themselves.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: There have been more and more 'accidents' lately, ever since the businessmen and military announced the acquisition plan for this spot.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Can you really not tell who sent that fraud of a 'reporter'?

steps.name: Reporter's Voice
steps.text: ...As we can see, what the tenants call a 'cradle of art' is nothing more than a collection of fire hazards.

steps.name: Reporter's Voice
steps.text: Many upstanding members of society are willing to take up the rebuilding of this art community, and do their part for the development of Dossoles.

steps.name: Reporter's Voice
steps.text: The military, in particular, is leading the charge...

steps.name: Obsequious Soldier
steps.text: Bravo, Captain Mateo! Even those hoodlums wouldn't dare cross the line now that the press has its eyes on them.

steps.name: Mateo
steps.text: Hmph. The money-grubbers think all we know is how to shoot a gun, that we'd be no match for them when it comes to the acquisition plan.

steps.name: Mateo
steps.text: But I've got much more experience than they do in dealing with those troublemakers of the art community.

steps.name: Obsequious Soldier
steps.text: You said it, sir.

steps.name: Mateo
steps.text: If that reporter does his job, we'll drive these worthless tramps out of the community without having to pay compensation.

steps.name: Mateo
steps.text: They may put on a tough face, but deep in their hearts, they thirst for recognition. Let's see what they think they can do, once we burn their nest to the ground.

steps.name: Obsequious Soldier
steps.text: Your cunning is matched only by your courage, sir! It's just a matter of time before that land is ours.

steps.name: Reporter's Voice
steps.text: ...This selfish, immoral behavior endangers the homes of countless innocent citizens.

steps.name: Reporter's Voice
steps.text: Here we have a child who was just rescued from the fire. Let's ask her how she feels.

steps.name: Reporter's Voice
steps.text: Where are your mama and papa, little girl? Are you in pain?

steps.name: Restrained Voice
steps.text: Who are you calling... little girl...?

steps.name: Reporter's Voice
steps.text: No need to act tough, kiddo. We're here to show the world how terrible those scary hoodlums are. We'll help you get back home... ouch!

steps.name: Angry Voice
steps.text: Who are you calling 'little girl'?! You call yourself a reporter when you don't even know what a Durin looks like?!

steps.name: Reporter's Voice
steps.text: G-Get off me, you brat!

steps.name: Reporter's Voice
steps.text: Turn off the camera, you idiot! Pull this psycho off me!

steps.name: Cameraman's Voice
steps.text: O-Okay!

steps.name: Mateo
steps.text: Hmph... they're tough, I'll give them that.

steps.name: Obsequious Soldier
steps.text: Y-You're absolutely right, sir.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Ugh... that kid sure was strong for her size.

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: Sir, I can't get the interior of the club from this angle.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: You've got legs for a reason. If you can't shoot it from the outside, go in.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: The fire's been burning for a few hours since we started shooting. They managed to put the one at the club out, but the two neighboring apartments aren't so lucky.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Ha! All the better. The bigger the fire, the more sensational the photos, and the more likely this will make the headlines!

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Hold it right there.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Sorry about that. We just want a couple of photos for a Society Tribune special. We'll leave once we have them.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Don't think I'm oblivious to your scheme. You use our charred artwork to grab attention, then turn the public against us to drive us out!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Now, now, what's with the slandering? How often does your, er, 'artwork' get a chance to be seen in newspapers and TV?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: It's great exposure. You might even get famous, if you're lucky!

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: What kind of artist would happily subject her artwork, that she poured her heart and soul into, to the fires of the media?!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Heart and soul? Pfft. This trash you call 'artwork' was a disaster even before the fire! If anything, it's an improvement—

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: You don't know anything about art!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Sure, I'm just an ordinary viewer, but viewers have the right to their opinions too.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Clumsy brushwork, rough effects... even a third-rate amusement park's haunted house wouldn't take this crap.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: At least now it has some value.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: After all, isn't it you artists who say that ashes are beautiful too?

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: How dare you!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Get out of my way. You can't stop me.

steps.name: Diaz
steps.text: I believe I can.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: You're the fireman who came to fight the fire on his own?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: So noble! Here's my card. Please, give me a call if you're interested in doing an exclusive.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Now, if you would excuse me...

steps.name: Diaz
steps.text: The scene has not yet been secured.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Diaz
steps.text: A comprehensive check is required to prevent secondary damage. We request your cooperation with firefighting efforts.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: As far as I know... the fire department doesn't have any personnel assigned to the art community. You're overstepping, don't you think?

steps.name: Diaz
steps.text: And as far as I know, electric sparks don't make clean cuts like these, aging circuits or not. Besides, I don't think our reporters are this... efficient, don't you think?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: This isn't over.

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: Umm, sir? Why did the streetlights go out? It's pitch black here... I'm starting to get the creeps.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: This is all the fault of that stupid firefighter. We'll go once we've got our photos of the scene.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Let's see how smug these hoodlums are when photos of their 'artwork' are all over the press.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Hey, where's the club? Did we take a wrong turn?

a.text: A musbeast dashes past their feet in the dark alley.
In his fright, the rookie cameraman accidentally turns on the camera light, illuminating a rugged concrete wall.

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: Sticky red liquid... it's still dripping... C-Could it be...?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Hmph! Those hoodlums splatter a few geometric figures with red paint and call themselves avant-garde. And they say I'm the one who doesn't know anything about art.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Art is not about form, but how it evokes emotions.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Joy, sorrow, anger, fear... true art strips away all the masks that the viewer is wearing, commanding total immersion with its power.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: A height these people will never reach.

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: I didn't know you were such a connoisseur.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: You saw how things were during the day. Those artists are like walking Catastrophes. Who knows what they'd do if they caught us?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: I've already arranged with the station to get the video on air as soon as the storage card arrives. And we'll get our 'bonus' once Captain Mateo sees it.

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: Good call!

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: Wh-What's that sound?!

steps.name: Sound from Left Window
steps.text: Come on, boy, look at the time, you should be in bed... my eyelids are drooping...

steps.name: Sound from Left Window
steps.text: The fire really spooked him, dear. Be patient.

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Look at you, getting all riled up over a couple putting their boy to bed.

steps.name: Sound from Left Window
steps.text: The owner of the club said it was arson.

steps.name: Sound from Left Window
steps.text: I'll wring the neck of whoever did it. Look how our baby's hair got singed...

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: Baby...

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: You're not scared of a little kid, are you?

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: No... I mean... there's a kid standing on the corner... and it seems to be... glowing?

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: But the moon isn't out!

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: Wh-What is it? Why is it looking at us?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: S-Stop letting everything scare you! Can't you see it's not moving? Probably some scrap the hoodlums left here.

a.text: The words have barely left his mouth when the 'child' innocently cocks its head, at an angle that should not be possible.
One step, two steps... it, or 'he' starts running towards them with an eerie smile on his face.

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: D-Do normal children run that fast?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: L-Let's get out of here for now...

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: ...Intern?

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: This is not what I expected for my first day on the job!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Why you son of a...! Wait for me! And don't you drop that camera!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: You're getting better and better at manipulating your puppets, Tecno.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Got to thank the painter couple that lives on the second floor. They were furious at the fright that the fire gave their pet fowlbeast.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Third-rate amusement park's haunted house, eh? We'll show them what artists can do when they're pissed.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Art is about evoking emotions, eh? We'll show them how art can evoke this little emotion called 'fear'.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Get the boys ready, Sullivan. We're just getting to the good part.

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: *pant* *pant* I... I wanna go home...

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: Papá says children killed by fire become angry ghosts! This one must be here for revenge!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Oh, shut up... W-We didn't do anything wrong...

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Are you out of your mind? Why are you laughing?! We won't get any pictures if we wake the locals!

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: It wasn't me! I-It's him... he's coming for us!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: I thought our wires burned in the fire. How did you get that sound?

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Turrión built a makeshift generator out of an exercise bike.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Cool!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: He's not submitting a new work for our project tonight?

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: He is. The title is 'Turrión on Bike'.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: His specialty is performance art, after all.

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: Dead end... We're done for...

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Pull yourself together! It's just some stupid parlor trick. Get your camera ready. We're getting that bonus from Captain Mateo!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: Aw! Ouch... Quit hiding behind me!

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: I-It wasn't me!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: I think... there's somebody... behind us...

a.text: It is the shadow they see first.
It stretches from their feet to the entrance of the alley, cutting off all possibility of escape.
The reporter can feel his neck go stiff. Still, he cannot help but turn his head to look and see just what terror awaits him.
He spies a horrifying visage, its terrible mouth gaping open, exuding a charred stench.
Its jaw creaks ominously as it opens and closes, delivering a chilling question from beyond the grave—

steps.name: Intern Cameraman & Reporter
steps.text: YESSSEEEEEEKKK—

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: I see. The sculpture's head is now driven by wind power rather than Originium, but the instability makes it feel even more alive.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Gotta give Turrión his due. The projections wouldn't have worked nearly as well, if not for him on the bike controlling the output.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: He should get a side job generating electricity.

steps.name: Street Sculptor
steps.text: And I should thank that reporter too. A complete amateur, but what he said about beauty did give me some new inspiration.

steps.name: Street Sculptor
steps.text: I salvaged the transmission from the club, while trying out some new things with the interplay of light and shadow.

steps.name: Street Sculptor
steps.text: I'm planning to submit this sculpture for next week's exhibit. I think it'll be a smash hit!

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Trying out new things...

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: You know, I've always been interested in all kinds of music.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: I know, Tecno, but I don't have the money to pay you back for the tickets right now.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: No, that's not what I meant...

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: What I mean is, are you up for a collab song?

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: What was that? Why do I feel like someone's whispering in my ear when there's no one there?!

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Hey, I like this synthesizer.

steps.name: Intern Cameraman
steps.text: M-My brain's all jumbled... Will we ever get out of this place?

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Hell yeah! You hear the eight bars of dissonance? Planned by yours truly.

steps.name: Intern Cameraman & Reporter
steps.text: HELLLLLLLP—

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Gotta hand it to you too, Tecno... Didn't know you could sound so... guttural!

steps.name: Reporter
steps.text: I see light! We're outta here! Screw Mateo's bonus!

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: *cough* I've wanted to try that forever.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: More into it now? I'll take you to my favorite heavy metal band's next gig. No excuses the next time we vote.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Deal! But only if you do my vocal sampling for my next track!

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Deal!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Hey, where did they go?
*pant*... *pant*... how did these two... *pant*... end up... *pant*... over here...?

steps.name: Turrión
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*... And... *pant* they're out cold...

steps.name: Turrión
steps.text: The conversion of... *pant* kinetic energy... *pant* into... *pant* electric energy... *pant*... is so tiring... *pant*... Tecno!

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Good work, Turrión.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: I knew I was right to save you for last.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Yikes, muchacho, you almost scared the daylights out of me!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: You look like a corpse that just got trawled out of a lake... what happened to your clothes?

steps.name: Turrión
steps.text: Hehe... *pant*... the sacrifices we make... *pant*... in the name of art...

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: What do we do now?

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: You know, screams aside, this kid's pretty handy with a camera.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: It's not often the community comes together to put on a show like this. It'd be a shame if only two people got to see it.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Hey, didn't they say they would put the video on air as soon as it arrived?

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Tecno? What are you doing by yourself here when everyone else is celebrating at the party?

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: You see the reaction to the broadcast?

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Absurdist, horror, farce... people are calling it all sorts of things, but at least the TV station won't be back for a very long time.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Doesn't mean we can rest easy, though.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: There are a lot of people with designs on our turf. They don't see value in street art; all they want to do is to run this bunch of 'unproductive vagrants' out of town.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Yeah... Today's party is a farewell for some of us.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: It's tough enough that doing art costs so much with so little recognition in return. If we also have to constantly fear for our safety, things will get really hard...

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: At this rate, who knows when the club will reopen again...

steps.name: Curious Tourist
steps.text: Excuse me...

steps.name: Curious Tourist
steps.text: Are you the street artists from the late-night show on TV?

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: That's us.

steps.name: Curious Tourist
steps.text: Wow! Can I get a picture with you? My friends and I love the artwork in that short!

steps.name: Curious Tourist
steps.text: I'm not an artist, so I can't explain why I like them with technical terms. But I can feel certain emotions, like the release of pent-up frustration and a sense of self-mockery... Sorry if I got any of that wrong...

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: You... you really do like our artwork?

steps.name: Curious Tourist
steps.text: Yes!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Which piece is your favorite?

steps.name: Curious Tourist
steps.text: My favorite...?

steps.name: Curious Tourist
steps.text: Hey, what's with all the people...?

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Please give us a sec.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Good thing the scoreboard survived the fire.

steps.name: Tecno
steps.text: Voting is not over yet, friends. Just because my choice of music didn't win doesn't mean my artwork won't!

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Our artwork.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: If you like the mix track, cast your vote for the first and last numbers.

steps.name: Sullivan
steps.text: Here, girl, take the drill.

steps.name: Curious Tourist
steps.text: So cool! Is this some kind of new interactive installation?

steps.name: Street Sculptor
steps.text: Just a little idea of mine.

steps.name: Street Sculptor
steps.text: By the way, if you like the sculpture over there, vote for the number in the middle.

a.text: In front of the collapsed club, the worn-out music player continues to play back the peculiar collab track, attracting a crowd of onlookers.
Tecno brings out her little puppets for her campaign, while the Sculptor scribbles on the ground with chalk.
Pepe Turrión is about to take off his clothes again, but is stopped by the other artists.
Holding each other's hands, two charred little puppets dance around the feet of the crowd to the background music.
If I make the puppets bigger, perhaps they'll reach more eyes, Tecno mused. Maybe then, I'll discover there are more people out there who truly understand us.
One day, they will dance on a bigger stage.
